validation.integration: Added an opt-in native CPU coroutine-frame guard, inspired by the reviewed SotC quarantine technique but implemented for macOS. The renderer's actual Task promise allocates independent mappings when SOTC_TASK_GUARD=1. Existing ordered recording-consumer retirement remains unchanged; deletion makes that frame's pages PROT_NONE and retains up to 64 frames within an 8 MiB total live/quarantine mapping budget. This does not retain or change guest objects/pages or GPU resource ownership. Budget/slot/allocation exhaustion uses normal new/delete, explicitly recorded as unguarded fallback. Protection/unmap failures preserve owned mapping accounting and report incomplete coverage; no false release. A separate task-events.bin retains 256 allocations/fallbacks and 256 retirement/ unmap/failure events, with address, rounded/requested size, generation, thread, current budget and counters. Offline diagnostics match a fault address to the latest retained mapping event only as a candidate, excluding foreign producer PIDs. Reuse/finite retention, fallback and eviction can hide lifetime bugs. The journal adds 68 KiB (all files 784 KiB when enabled), plus bounded host metadata and at most 8 MiB of frame mappings; not a total process-memory limit. No native corruption correction or overhead measurement is established. Runtime default remains disabled; the owner diagnostic launcher defaults the guard on, with explicit SOTC_TASK_GUARD=0 opting out. All persistent source/header and indexed referring-object probes remain active; the guard tests CPU renderer frames, not whether the failing PS4 object is alive. The new command explicitly sets SOTC_TASK_GUARD=1. No game/GPU test was launched. Original CPU controls use the actual production Task/retirement helper: valid ordered consumers pass, premature and later stale reads trap on real protected pages. Budget fallback, quarantine rotation, concurrency, injected protection/ unmap failures and stale-PID rejection are checked. Existing delayed-consumer ASan controls remain. Repeated native protected-reader tests confirm PROT_NONE reads fail without changing kernel permissions. The renderer builds ARM64 with all builder CPU regressions; cache remains 28/9. Exact task_guard_previous cohort migration and idempotence checks pass. Dependencies stay pinned. Its diff is reviewed and not adopted as a lifetime fix. Other checked default heads unchanged; previous PR/release and object-method limits retained. Full ARM64 JIT/interpreter contracts, nine guard cases, ten pointer tests, four protected-reader tests, fourteen reports, twenty-six builder tests and 46/46 symbols pass; native validation pending.
